# Select volume merge — `volumes_compiled_select.R`

**Selection:** Stephan-collection core + de Sousa/Matano/Zilles/Bauernfeind/MacLeod/Smaers
**Tables:** 32 | **Teams:** 1 | **Result:** 65 species x 86 variables | **Tie rule:** `first` | **Mass rule:** `reference` | **Taxa:** `Order = Primates`

> This block is hand-written (`README__volumes_compiled_select.INTRO.md`) and is spliced into the
> generated README on every run. Everything below it is regenerated — edit this file, not that one.

## What this is

A third sibling to `volumes_compiled.R` (the full collection) and `volumes_compiled_DeCasien.R`
(the DeCasien subset): a merge of a **hand-chosen** set of tables, treated as **one evolving
dataset**, where the most recent measurement of each species x structure supersedes the older ones
— *except* where a value has been flagged as one that must not be used, however recent it is.

Three files make it work, and only these three should ever need editing:

| File | What it controls |
|---|---|
| `volumes_compiled_select.R` → `select_datasets` | which tables are in, what team each belongs to, and the year used for recency |
| `volumes_select_value_flags.csv` | which individual values are vetoed, reviewed, or explicitly kept |
| `README__volumes_compiled_select.INTRO.md` | this prose |

Everything else — the merge, the audit CSVs, and the rest of this README — is regenerated.

## The value-flag registry

`volumes_select_value_flags.csv` has seven columns:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Source` | item name. Exact, or `*` for all, or a trailing-`*` prefix match (`Stephan_etal_1981_Table*`) |
| `Species` | resolved (accepted) species name, or `*` / blank for all |
| `Variable` | standardized term, or `*` / blank for all, or a prefix match (`Area_striata_*`) |
| `flag` | short tag that groups the entry in this README (`secondary_compilation`, `derived_residual`, `unverifiable`, `taxonomy_lump`, …) |
| `action` | `skip` = never use this value, however recent · `review` = use it but list it here · `keep` = explicitly un-skip, to carve an exception out of a broader `skip` row |
| `reason` | prose. This is what gets printed in the "why" blocks below, so write it for a reader |
| `evidence` | where the decision is documented (a findings file, a registry column, a paper) |

The **most specific** matching row wins (`Source` beats `Species` beats `Variable`); among equally
specific rows, the one **last in the file** wins. A `skip` is applied *before* the recency pick, so
the next-most-recent unflagged value takes over — and if nothing else covers the cell, the variable
simply drops out of the merge and says so below.

## Decisions baked into version 1 of the selection

- **Smaers et al. 2017 is in, but six of its eight columns are vetoed.** It is the newest table, so
  on recency alone it would supersede everything it touches — but `crosspub_Smaers2017_FINDINGS.md`
  and the `Flags pre-addressed` column of `__ReadMe.xlsx` establish that it is a compilation.
  `primary_visual` is Frahm et al. 1984's area striata (value-matched exact), `prefrontal` is Smaers
  et al. 2011 Suppl. Table 2, `other_association` is a derived residual. Only `frontal_motor`
  survives, flagged `review` because it was never published anywhere it can be checked.
  Its numbers are printed as mm³ but are cm³ — the reshape multiplies by 1000.
- **de Sousa 2010 is Table 1 only.** Supplementary Table 2 carries a known value error (neocortex
  mis-copied from Stephan 1981 for 17 strepsirrhine/tarsier species; 13 of them exceed brain volume).
  Add it to `select_datasets` with a `skip` row on its neocortex column if you need its bilateral
  V1/LGN means.
- **de Sousa 2010's left-only V1 and LGN are not doubled.** Step 7 turns one-side volumes into
  both-sides ones, but `bilateral_stems_exclude` holds these two back, because the paper's own
  Supplementary Table 2 has the real bilateral means. Remove them from that vector to let the 2x
  estimate through (it would be flagged, never silent).
- **Same-year ties go to the earlier row in `select_datasets`.** MacLeod 2003 Table 1 (Yerkes) and
  Table 2 (Hirnforschung) are different samples of the same year; Table 1 is listed first, so it
  wins for the nine species in both. Set `tie_rule <- "mean"` to average them instead — every tie is
  listed below either way.
- **Body and brain mass stay pinned to Stephan 1981 Tables I–III**, as in `volumes_compiled.R`; set
  `mass_rule <- "recent"` to treat them like any other variable.
- **Species names resolve exactly as in the full merge** (curated overrides beat NCBI, source-aware).
  Unlike `volumes_compiled.R` this script never rewrites `volumes_species_ids_cache.csv`, and a name
  the cache has not seen is a warning rather than a hard stop.

## Running it

    Rscript volumes_compiled_select.R          # or open in RStudio and Source

Needs the full repo (it reads `__ReadMe.xlsx`, `__Public/comparative-data/` and `_keys/`), plus
`tidyverse` and `readxl`. `taxizedb` is optional — without it the committed NCBI cache is used.
`_verify_volumes_compiled_select.py` is an offline mirror of the same logic for checking the
resolution on a machine without R; `volumes_compiled_select.R` is authoritative.

## The rule

Every selected table is collapsed to one value per species x structure, then resolved **within a
team by most recent year**. A candidate flagged `skip` in `volumes_select_value_flags.csv` is
removed **before** that pick, so the next-most-recent unflagged value wins instead. Across teams
(only if the selection names more than one) surviving values are averaged, as in `volumes_compiled.R`.

## Values used but flagged `review`

Kept in the merge, but the registry says they need eyes.

**`unit_suspect`** — 13 value(s)

> Scale check: the TSV column brain_mass_mg really is milligrams (Pan paniscus 395000 = 395 g; Alouatta caraya 55800 = 55.8 g), but the reshape divides by 1000, so the value carried under the term Brain_Mass.mg is in GRAMS - 1000x smaller than the term claims. This comes from volumes_compiled.R (same line, same result in the canonical volumes_long.csv), so it is an upstream issue, NOT something this selection introduced. Here it only reaches the 13 species Stephan 1981 does not cover, because mass_rule pins the rest to Stephan. Set action to skip, or fix the reshape upstream, once decided.

_Sources:_ Bauernfeind_etal_2013_Table1  
_Variables:_ Brain_Mass.mg  
_Species:_ Alouatta caraya, Cebuella pygmaea, Cercocebus agilis, Colobus angolensis, Hylobates muelleri, Leontopithecus rosalia, Macaca maura, Pan paniscus, Pithecia pithecia, Pongo sp., Saguinus geoffroyi, Symphalangus syndactylus, Trachypithecus francoisi

**`unverifiable`** — 19 value(s)

> frontal_motor_gray is the only genuinely 2017-unique numeric column, so it is kept - but it is the POSTERIOR section-5 of 20 frontal sections and was never published anywhere else, so it cannot be checked against any public table. It is a biased anterior/posterior proxy, not the true premotor border. Treat as provisional. Re-checked 2026-08-12: frontal_motor is NOT the complement of prefrontal within the lobe - prefrontal + frontal_motor sums to only 32-47% of Smaers 2011 total frontal grey (53-68% short in all 19 spp.), so total frontal grey cannot be reconstructed from the two subregions. It is now carried directly as FrontalCortex_grey_matter_Vol.mm3 from Smaers_etal_2011_SupplementaryTable1.

_Sources:_ Smaers_etal_2017_TableS1part1  
_Variables:_ FrontalMotor_grey_matter_Vol.mm3  
_Species:_ Alouatta seniculus, Ateles geoffroyi, Cebus albifrons, Cercopithecus ascanius, Cercopithecus mitis, Erythrocebus patas, Gorilla sp., Homo sapiens, Hylobates lar, Lagothrix lagothricha, Lophocebus albigena, Miopithecus talapoin, Nasalis larvatus, Pan paniscus, Pan troglodytes, Papio anubis, Piliocolobus badius, Pithecia pithecia, Pongo sp.

**`unverifiable`** — 19 value(s)

> frontal_motor_white is the white-matter counterpart of the same unpublished posterior section-5 partition: 2017-unique, kept, but unverifiable against any public table and a proxy rather than a true premotor border.

_Sources:_ Smaers_etal_2017_TableS1part1  
_Variables:_ FrontalMotor_white_matter_Vol.mm3  
_Species:_ Alouatta seniculus, Ateles geoffroyi, Cebus albifrons, Cercopithecus ascanius, Cercopithecus mitis, Erythrocebus patas, Gorilla sp., Homo sapiens, Hylobates lar, Lagothrix lagothricha, Lophocebus albigena, Miopithecus talapoin, Nasalis larvatus, Pan paniscus, Pan troglodytes, Papio anubis, Piliocolobus badius, Pithecia pithecia, Pongo sp.

**`zero_sentinel`** — 17 value(s)

> Stephan 1981 prints 0 for the nucleus tractus olfactorius in several catarrhines. Per the Stephan 1987 data dictionary a printed 0 means 'not determinable with certainty', not a true zero - volumes_compiled.R maps it to NA for the 1987 table but leaves the 1981 zeros standing, and so does this script (5 species end up with NTO = 0). Decide whether the 1981 zeros are sentinels too before using this variable; contrast Bulbus_olfactorius_accessorius, whose zeros in catarrhines are real absences.

_Sources:_ Stephan_etal_1981_TableXI  
_Variables:_ Nucleus_tractus_olfactorius_Vol.mm3  
_Species:_ Alouatta seniculus, Aotus trivirgatus, Callithrix jacchus, Cebus albifrons, Cercopithecus ascanius, Cheirogaleus major, Cheirogaleus medius, Daubentonia madagascariensis, Eulemur fulvus, Galagoides demidoff, Homo sapiens, Lepilemur ruficaudatus, Microcebus murinus, Piliocolobus badius, Propithecus verreauxi, Saimiri sciureus, Tarsius sp.

## Hemisphere reconciliation (step 7)

Both-sides partners built for: `Agranular_insular_cortex`, `Dysgranular_insular_cortex`, `Granular_insular_cortex`, `Insula`, `fronto_insular_cortex`.
Excluded by `bilateral_stems_exclude`: `Area_striata_grey_matter`, `Corpus_geniculatum_laterale`.
`316` value(s) are 2x estimates from a single measured side, doubled **by this merge** (flag `estimated_bilateral_from_unilateral` in `volumes_flags_select.csv`).

`19` value(s) arrive **already doubled by the source** — the authors published 2x one hemisphere with a stated symmetry argument, so the figure is used as published and never doubled again (flag `published_bilateral_estimate`; registered as `doubling = by_source` in `laterality_known.csv`).

Neither flag is a veto. Both record how a both-sides number came to exist; a value is only ever removed by an `action = skip` row in `volumes_select_value_flags.csv`.

## Files written

- `volumes_long_select.csv` — merged long table (the result)
- `volumes_wide_select.csv` — species x variable matrix
- `volumes_flags_select.csv` — bilateral-estimate provenance from steps 7 and 7b (`estimated_bilateral_from_unilateral`, `published_bilateral_estimate`); neither is a veto
- `volumes_unfiltered_select.csv` — every value read, before resolution
- `volumes_resolution_audit_select.csv` — every candidate: USED / superseded / skipped
- `volumes_flagged_not_used_select.csv` — machine-readable version of the table above
- `volumes_taxon_excluded_select.csv` — species removed by the taxon filter, with why
- `volumes_source_species_ids_select.csv` — species-name resolution for sign-off
- `volumes_species_sources_select.csv` — which sources contributed each species
- `README__volumes_compiled_select.md` — this file

## Changing the selection

1. Edit the `select_datasets` tribble in `volumes_compiled_select.R` (item / team / year).
2. If a table is new to the merge, give it a term map:
   `standardized_term_by_reference/<Item>_standardized_terms.csv` (picked up automatically).
3. Add any value vetoes to `volumes_select_value_flags.csv`.
4. Re-run. Nothing else needs editing — this README is regenerated.
